issues.legal_issue: An unconditional undertaking to vacate given to obtain time, followed by reliance on extensions, may make a later challenge to the merits an abuse of process when the circumstances show that the litigant had agreed to rest content with time to vacate.
material_facts: The litigants gave an unconditional undertaking to vacate after the appellate court indicated that the appeal against the possession decree lacked merit.
They obtained time to vacate on the basis of the undertaking and later obtained a further extension to find other premises.
They subsequently sought review and pursued a further challenge to the possession decree.
issues.conclusion: In the circumstances, the litigants could not use their undertaking and the extensions obtained on its basis while also pursuing a challenge to the merits; doing so was an abuse of process.
issues.legal_principle: Under P R Deshpande v. Maruti Balaram Haibatti, (1998) 6 SCC 507, an undertaking given as a condition for a stay does not, by itself, foreclose a statutory or constitutional remedy, including a remedy under Article 136 of the Constitution. But that principle does not protect a litigant who sought and obtained time to vacate, and whose conduct shows that the undertaking was not given to preserve occupation while pursuing a further challenge; using that undertaking and its benefits to prolong a merits challenge may constitute abuse of process.

rule.if: appeal_against_possession_decree and unconditional_vacate_undertaking_for_time and benefit_of_extensions_taken and conduct_showed_settling_for_time_to_vacate

predicates.appeal_against_possession_decree: The litigant appealed a judgment ordering possession of premises.
predicates.unconditional_vacate_undertaking_for_tim: The litigant unconditionally promised to vacate in order to obtain time to do so.
predicates.benefit_of_extensions_taken: The litigant obtained and used extensions of the time to vacate on the basis of the undertaking.
predicates.conduct_showed_settling_for_time_to_vaca: The litigant sought time to vacate and further extensions before later pursuing a challenge to the merits.

issues.definition: When a litigant appealing a possession decree unconditionally promises to vacate for time, uses extensions, and conducts the matter as one seeking time to vacate, a later merits challenge is treated as an abuse of process.

issues.legal_issue: A litigant who occupied premises under a conducting arrangement rather than a licence could not acquire tenancy status on the basis of the asserted conversion of that licence.
material_facts: The trial court found, relying on the litigant's admissions and supporting records, that the business and premises had been given under a conducting arrangement.
An earlier proceeding had found that the arrangement did not create a licensor-licensee relationship.
The litigant nevertheless argued that its status as a licensee had later become that of a tenant.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy-status argument was rejected because there was no licence in the litigant's favour that could have developed into tenancy status.
issues.legal_principle: The court relied on the factual findings in the possession suit and the earlier proceeding, including admissions that the premises and business were given under a conducting arrangement. In the absence of a licence and a licensor-licensee relationship, the litigant could not claim that its status as a licensee had become that of a tenant.

predicates.possession_suit_involving_claimed_tenanc: A possession suit involved a litigant's claim that an earlier licence had developed into tenancy status.
predicates.conducting_arrangement_established: The evidence, including the litigant's admissions, showed that the premises and business were provided under a conducting arrangement.
predicates.no_licensor_licensee_relationship_found: A court found that the arrangement did not create a relationship between a licensor and a licensee.

issues.definition: A claimed conversion from licence to tenancy is rejected in a possession suit when the evidence establishes a conducting arrangement and a court has found no licensor-licensee relationship.

issues.legal_issue: Delay in filing special leave petitions may be condoned when the litigants pursued review before the High Court.
material_facts: The special leave petitions were filed late.
Before approaching the Supreme Court, the litigants had sought review before the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The delay in the special leave petitions was condoned.
issues.legal_principle: The court condoned the delay because the litigants had moved the High Court in review; the judgment cites no separate provision or earlier case for this determination.

predicates.delayed_special_leave_petitions: The litigants filed special leave petitions after the applicable filing time had elapsed.
predicates.high_court_review_pursued: The litigants sought review of the challenged orders before the High Court.

issues.definition: When special leave petitions are delayed and the litigants have pursued review before the High Court, the filing delay is condoned.

issues.legal_issue: Courts should impose exemplary costs to deter frivolous proceedings that abuse judicial process and consume resources needed for genuine cases.
material_facts: The litigants obtained an initial period and a further extension to vacate, then sought review and a much longer extension while continuing to challenge the possession decree.
The Supreme Court found the proceedings frivolous and an abuse of process, and observed that they prolonged a stale dispute and consumed court time.
issues.conclusion: The court imposed exemplary costs on the litigants.
issues.legal_principle: The court stated that it is the duty of courts to deal firmly with frivolous filings and abuse of process. Exemplary, real costs are a necessary instrument to deter litigation designed to benefit from delay, protect judicial resources, and preserve access to courts for genuine causes. No earlier case or specific statutory provision was cited for this principle.

predicates.court_proceeding_involving_possession_di: A court proceeding concerned a dispute over possession of premises.
predicates.repeated_extensions_used: The litigant obtained more than one extension of time to vacate the premises.
predicates.frivolous_challenges_prolonged_dispute: The litigant pursued challenges that the court found frivolous and that prolonged the dispute.

issues.definition: When repeated extensions and frivolous challenges prolong a possession dispute, exemplary costs are imposed.
